summary.what: The typeface comes in four families (01, 03, 06, 09) across 18 styles, supporting Latin and Cyrillic character sets with a variable font version for morphing geometry.

articles.decoder: * **Grotesque**: A classification of sans-serif typefaces characterized by high legibility, low contrast between stroke weights, and subtle humanist details.

articles.title: Designing a better future: your guide to design contribution in Open Source
articles.description: Open-source projects often lack the UX expertise needed to make powerful software approachable, while designers struggle to discover contribution opportunities in developer-oriented environments such as GitHub. Meaningful contributions can include user research, clearer project descriptions, onboarding improvements, navigation, error messages, accessibility, and better documentation of design processes rather than just visual assets. Designers can begin by exploring projects they already use, reviewing contribution guidelines, finding relevant issues, and collaborating directly with maintainers, even without extensive technical knowledge.
articles.one-liner: Designers are increasingly needed to bridge the usability gap in open-source software, focusing on user research and onboarding rather than just iconography.

summary.what: Canonical’s design team outlines how non-technical contributors can impact projects by improving documentation, error messages, user navigation, and onboarding flows via GitHub.
summary.why: Open-source projects often lack the UX maturity of proprietary software; professional design input is critical to improving user adoption and creating viable alternatives to closed-source tools.
summary.takeaway: Browse 'contribute.design' or 'opensourcedesign.net' to find active open-source projects explicitly seeking design help if you want to make your first contribution.

articles.deep-summary:
* Designers often struggle with the technical barrier of Git/GitHub.
* Non-code contributions like user research and process documentation are as impactful as visual assets.
* User adoption rates correlate strongly with UX and intuitive design.
* Maintainers often need guidance on how to define design tasks.
* The Open Design movement aims to integrate design workflows into the software development lifecycle.
* Beginners should focus on improving 'empty states' and error messages in familiar tools.
articles.decoder:
* **Forking**: Creating a personal copy of a project repository on a platform like GitHub, allowing a contributor to propose changes without affecting the original codebase until a pull request is accepted.
* **Pull Request (PR)**: A mechanism for a contributor to propose changes to a project's codebase that the maintainer can review and merge.

articles.one-liner: German artist Vin Clovercreek creates luminous, atmospheric paintings that explore themes of friendship and wanderlust through soft, dreamlike color palettes.

articles.title: Figma Adds Version History for AI Plugins and Shaders
articles.description: Every edit now saves a new version with an agent-generated description, while earlier ones stay available to review and restore.
articles.one-liner: Figma is introducing granular version history for generative plugins and shaders, allowing designers to roll back changes with agent-generated descriptions.

summary.what: Figma’s update enables creators to save, review, and restore previous iterations of generative tools and shaders, featuring automated descriptions for each edit and a specific indicator for the currently published version.
summary.why: As generative design tools move from experimentation to production-grade workflows, native version control becomes essential for debugging complex custom shaders or prompt-based plugin logic.

articles.deep-summary:
* Automatically generated descriptions track changes across iterations of custom generative tools.
* Users can restore older versions of plugins and shaders if new outputs are suboptimal.
* A dedicated indicator highlights which version is currently live for users, separating it from ongoing experimental edits.
* The feature aims to solve the fragility inherent in iterative generative design workflows.
articles.decoder: * **Shader**: A program, typically written in GLSL or HLSL, that instructs the graphics processing unit (GPU) on how to calculate color, light, and shading for digital imagery.
